_doc: WEBER dating cabinet (#43, Wave E, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #50). Carl B. Weber's Jersey City factory — an American middle-market GIANT and the great PRIVATE-LABEL engine (Wilke, Barclay Rex, Trinity East and countless shop brands after 1950; also made Custombilt for Wally Frank/Hollco 1974-87 and owned Jobey in the 70s). Company end date UNDOCUMENTED -> wide honest ceilings. SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Weber_Pipe_Co_.json (+ Custom-Bilt.json + Jobey.json cross-facts).

history_anchors._doc: Carl B. Weber: Bavarian, emigrated 1911 aged 21. 1938: WEBER BRIARS INC, Jersey City NJ (later renamed Weber Pipe Co). Middle price/quality giant; trademark 'Weber' in an OVAL. Post-1950: THE private-label supplier — identical pipes at Wilke's, Barclay Rex, Trinity East, Northampton (Queens), Don-Lou (Brooklyn)...; most Wilke pipes = unstained Webers. Anthony Passante (d.1994; NOT Tony Pesante) worked there. STREAMLINER = c.1941 (Wayne Leser patent 1941; non-briar versions exist). 'The Scoop' (+ Scoop Junior sets), Golden Walnut, Deep Grain lines. Rogers pipes/accessory connection (Rodgers-Custombilt orbit). 1970s: owned by HOLLCO ROHR; made JOBEY (Tinder Box era) + CUSTOMBILT (1974-87, Grecian briar) at the NJ factory. Factory end: after the 1987 Custombilt move to France the trail goes cold — closure undocumented.

brand_marks.physical: 'Weber' in an oval = the trademark. Private-label output usually carries the SHOP's name, not Weber's — attribution to Weber needs shape/finish matching (e.g. the 'Wilke Danish Bent'), never assume.

line_years._notes: streamliner: c.1941 patent (Leser) -> [1940,1960] wide-approx (run length unknown). The Scoop / Golden Walnut / Deep Grain undated.
